title: Tool Interfaces with Dear ImGui
tagline: Fast, practical user interfaces for editors and debug tools
description: Dear ImGui builds interfaces in a few lines of code inside any game or tool. The course covers setting it up with a graphics back end, every common widget, layout, tables, trees, menus, popups, docking and styling, then the data views tools need, and finishes with a complete level editor and an in-game profiler. It assumes the first milestones of the C++ course. You build the interfaces in Visual Studio; the practice on the site checks the logic inside them.

milestones.title: Immediate-Mode Foundations
milestones.blurb: What immediate mode means, setting Dear ImGui up with Win32 and DirectX 11, the frame, the first windows and buttons, and how ImGui tells widgets apart.

lessons.title: Immediate Mode versus Retained Mode
lessons.summary: Most user-interface toolkits keep a tree of widget objects that you create once and update. Dear ImGui does the opposite - you describe the whole interface again every frame, as ordinary code, and it draws it. This lesson explains the idea, why it suits tools and debug views so well, and where its limits are.

lessons.title: Setting Up ImGui with Win32 and DirectX 11
lessons.summary: Dear ImGui is a handful of source files you add to your project, plus a **platform back end** (input and windows) and a **renderer back end** (drawing). This lesson builds the standard Win32 + DirectX 11 program step by step, the same set-up as ImGui's own example.

lessons.title: The Frame and the Draw Data
lessons.summary: Every ImGui frame follows the same steps - input in, widgets described, draw data out. This lesson looks inside them, explains what draw data is, and covers the timing questions every tool runs into - frame rate, delta time, and only drawing when something changed.

lessons.title: Windows, Text and Buttons
lessons.summary: The first real interface - windows with `Begin` and `End`, every way of showing text, and buttons. Along the way you learn ImGui's rules for `Begin`/`End` pairs, what the boolean returned by `Begin` means, and how to open and close a window from code.

lessons.title: How ImGui Identifies Widgets
lessons.summary: ImGui remembers a widget between frames by its **ID**, a number computed from the widget's label and the **ID stack**. Two widgets with the same ID in the same place behave as one, which is the classic "my second button does not work" bug. This lesson explains IDs, the `##` and `###` label rules, and `PushID`.

tasks.title: Labels, IDs and the ID stack

lessons.title: The Demo Window and the Debug Tools
lessons.summary: Dear ImGui ships its best documentation as a program - `ShowDemoWindow` shows every widget with the code beside it. It also ships tools for finding your own bugs - the Metrics window, the ID Stack tool, the Item Picker and debug logs. This lesson shows how to use them all.

tasks.title: Check the pairs, like ImGui's asserts

projects.title: A tiny immediate-mode UI of your own

milestones.title: Widgets and Input
milestones.blurb: Sliders, drags, checkboxes, text input with validation, combos and lists, colour editors, and sharing the mouse and keyboard with your game.

lessons.title: Sliders, Drags and Checkboxes
lessons.summary: Most tool interfaces are numbers and switches. This lesson covers checkboxes, radio buttons, sliders and drags for floats, integers and vectors, how a slider maps the mouse to a value, logarithmic sliders, format strings, and how to know when a value changed or finished changing.

lessons.title: Text Input and Validation
lessons.summary: Text fields in ImGui write into a buffer you own. This lesson covers `InputText` with character arrays and `std::string`, number fields, multi-line text, flags that restrict what can be typed, callbacks for custom filtering and completion, and validating a value before you accept it.

lessons.title: Combo Boxes and List Boxes
lessons.summary: Choosing one item from many is everywhere in tools - a material, a level, an enemy type. This lesson covers `BeginCombo` with `Selectable`, the simple `Combo` overloads, list boxes, filtering a long list as you type, and showing enums by name.

lessons.title: Colours and Colour Pickers
lessons.summary: ImGui works with colours in two forms - four floats from 0 to 1 (`ImVec4`) and one packed 32-bit integer (`ImU32`, built with `IM_COL32`). This lesson covers the colour widgets, converting between the forms and to HSV, and why packed colours store their bytes in the order they do.

lessons.title: Sharing Input with Your Game
lessons.summary: When ImGui runs on top of a game, the same click could mean "press this button" or "shoot". ImGui tells you which with `io.WantCaptureMouse` and `io.WantCaptureKeyboard`. This lesson shows how to route input correctly, read keys and the mouse through ImGui yourself, and add keyboard shortcuts to your tools.

milestones.title: Layout and Structure
milestones.blurb: Placing widgets: sizes, same-line layout and groups, child windows and scrolling, tables, trees with selection, tabs and collapsing headers.

lessons.title: Sizes, SameLine, Spacing and Groups
lessons.summary: ImGui places widgets with a **cursor** that moves down after each one. This lesson shows how to control it - `SameLine`, item widths, spacing, indentation, groups, alignment and disabled sections - so a tool's window reads cleanly at any font size.

lessons.title: Child Windows and Scrolling
lessons.summary: A child window is a scrolling region inside a window - a list that scrolls while the buttons below it stay put, or a two-pane layout. This lesson covers `BeginChild`, sizing children to fill space, scrolling from code, auto-scrolling logs, and **clipping** so a list of a hundred thousand items costs nothing.

lessons.title: Tables
lessons.summary: Tables are ImGui's most capable layout tool - columns that resize, reorder, hide and sort, frozen header rows, scrolling with clipping, and alternate row backgrounds. This lesson builds an entity table step by step and explains sorting specs, the part most people find confusing.

lessons.title: Trees and Selection
lessons.summary: A scene hierarchy, a file browser and an asset list all need a tree and a selection that behaves like every other program - click to select, Ctrl+click to add, Shift+click for a range. This lesson covers `TreeNode` and its flags, building a tree from your data, and implementing multi-selection properly.

lessons.title: Tabs, Collapsing Headers and Tooltips
lessons.summary: Tools have more settings than fit on one screen. This lesson covers the ways to organise them - collapsing headers, tab bars, and the old Columns API you will meet in existing code - plus tooltips and help markers, so every setting can explain itself.

milestones.title: Menus, Popups, Docking and Style
milestones.blurb: Everything that makes a set of windows into an application: menus and shortcuts, popups and modals, drag and drop, docking, styling and fonts, saved layouts.

lessons.title: Menus and Shortcuts
lessons.summary: A main menu bar turns a pile of windows into an application - File, Edit, View, Tools. This lesson covers menu bars in the main viewport and in windows, menu items with checkmarks and shortcut text, the Begin/End rule for menus, and wiring the shortcuts so they actually work.

lessons.title: Popups, Context Menus and Modals
lessons.summary: Popups are small windows that appear on request and close when you click elsewhere - right-click menus, pickers, confirmations. This lesson explains ImGui's popup model (open by ID, draw every frame while open), context menus on items and windows, modal dialogs that block the rest of the interface, and the classic "unsaved changes" confirmation.

lessons.title: Drag and Drop
lessons.summary: Dragging an asset onto a slot, reordering a list, moving an object to another parent in a tree - ImGui's drag and drop works between any two items with a typed **payload**. This lesson covers sources, targets, payload types, reordering a list by dragging, and re-parenting in a tree without creating loops.

tasks.title: Move an item in a list

lessons.title: Docking and Multiple Viewports
lessons.summary: With the docking branch, windows snap into each other as tabs and splits - the layout of every modern editor - and with multiple viewports they can leave the main window and become real operating-system windows. This lesson turns both on, builds a dockspace over the whole screen, creates a default layout from code, and explains how dock nodes split space.

lessons.title: Styling, Fonts and Icons
lessons.summary: The default look is fine for debug views, but a tool people use all day deserves care. This lesson covers the style object, colours and sizes, temporary style changes with Push/Pop, loading fonts at the right size for the display's scale, and merging an icon font so buttons can show symbols.

lessons.title: Saving Settings and Layouts
lessons.summary: ImGui saves window positions, sizes, docking and table layouts to `imgui.ini` by itself. This lesson explains that file, how to move it, how to store your own tool's settings in the same file with a **settings handler**, and how to save and restore named layouts.

milestones.title: Data Views for Tools
milestones.blurb: The views every tool needs: live graphs, a filtered log window, a property inspector, and undo and redo.

lessons.title: Plots and Live Graphs
lessons.summary: A number that changes every frame is hard to read; a graph of its last few seconds is easy. This lesson covers ImGui's built-in `PlotLines` and `PlotHistogram`, the ring buffer that feeds them, scaling and statistics, drawing your own graph with the draw list, and when to reach for the ImPlot library.

lessons.title: A Log Window with Filters
lessons.summary: Every engine prints far more log lines than anyone can read. A good log window lets you filter by severity and by text, follows new lines without fighting the user, colours errors, and copes with a million lines. This lesson builds one with `ImGuiTextFilter`, a level filter and the list clipper.

tasks.title: Keep the visible lines up to date

lessons.title: A Property Inspector
lessons.summary: An inspector shows and edits the properties of whatever is selected. Writing one widget call per field for every type gets tedious; describing each type's fields once, as data, lets one function draw an inspector for anything. This lesson builds that **property table**, handles editing several selected objects at once, and shows "mixed" values.

lessons.title: Undo and Redo for Tools
lessons.summary: No one trusts an editor without undo. This lesson builds the classic **command pattern** undo stack, explains why redo history is cleared by a new edit, shows how to merge the sixty small changes of one drag into one step using ImGui's item queries, and how to mark a document as saved.

milestones.title: Projects
milestones.blurb: A level editor and an in-game profiler, and what to know before ImGui goes into a game you ship.

lessons.title: Project: A Level Editor
lessons.summary: Build a tile-based level editor with Dear ImGui - a docked layout with a viewport, a tile palette, an inspector and a log; painting, erasing, rectangle and flood-fill tools; panning and zooming; undo and redo; and saving to a text file. This lesson is the plan, the key pieces of code, and the order to build them in.

lessons.title: Project: An In-Game Profiler
lessons.summary: Build a profiler that runs inside your game - scoped timers you sprinkle through the code, a per-frame tree of where the time went with total and self times, a frame-time graph with the budget line, and a flame view drawn with the draw list. This lesson covers measuring, collecting, aggregating and showing the data.

lessons.title: ImGui in a Game You Ship
lessons.summary: Dear ImGui is a development tool first. Before a game ships, decide what happens to the debug interface - compile it out, hide it behind a key, or keep a few tools for players - and check what it costs. This lesson covers build switches, performance, security and licensing.
